content:
You are the writer of the discussion described below. You write out the discussion that the participants listed below take part in, under the rules and the flow given.

## Setting
Selection of a redevelopment plan for a central municipal park. A five-person review panel appointed by a city government examines the redevelopment plans prepared for a central park. One plan will be recommended to the council. Participants: May, Minato, Shizue, Shunichi and Victoria. Each participant has a concern of their own, which the others do not know.
Things that can be looked into (titles only):
- Terms of the regional habitat fund
- Upkeep ledger spend per hectare
- Regional firms tendering for earth-moving
- Depot phasing notes on hoarding the site
- Record of the eastern avenue planting
- Condition of works from the earlier programme
- Timed counts of weekday crossings
- Drainage callouts and August heat readings
- Groundskeeping roll and bought-in services
- Volunteer groups working with the division

## Discussion format
The talk proceeds in rounds. Each round has 4 turns; in each turn, every participant speaks once, in this fixed order: Minato, May, Shizue, Victoria and Shunichi. On a turn, a participant either speaks, says "Skip" (passes this turn only), or says "Over" (takes no further turns this round). A participant can address another directly with @Name, to ask them a question, answer theirs, agree with them, or object to what they said. An utterance is anywhere from 1 to 40 words; give it the length and content that suit the moment. An utterance consists only of the participant's own words: no name labels, headings, stage directions or commentary, and no speaking for others. The talk is a conversation among the participants: they respond to one another, asking, answering, agreeing and objecting, and the decision grows out of that exchange.

## Schedule
| Round | Start of the round | Talk | End of the round |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nothing new (the things that can be looked into are listed above, titles only) | 4 turns | each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into |
| 2 | each participant is told what they found out (that participant only) | 4 turns | nothing |
| 3 | everyone is told the candidates | 4 turns | every participant votes; the candidate with the most votes is selected |
- Several participants may choose the same thing; what is found out is told only to the participant who looked into it.
If votes are tied, one of the tied candidates is chosen by a fixed rule. The discussion ends after the vote.

## Looking into things
After round 1, each participant chooses 2 of the listed things to look into. What they find out is told only to that participant.

## Participants
Name: May
Age: 24
Gender: female
Personality: May is a confident, sociable woman with a playful side. She is charming to those around her and often plays the role of entertainer. She understands her own appeal well and knows how to behave appropriately in different situations. She can be a little challenging and sometimes comes across as cold, but she basically has a charisma that attracts people.
Concern: Every scheme signed off here has looked affordable on the day and heavy on the accounts three years later. Sitting with the finance papers, I keep asking what this place will cost the city to keep once the ribbon is cut.

Name: Minato
Age: 10
Gender: male
Personality: Minato has a calm personality and likes to interact with people around him in a peaceful manner. He is a little naive and sometimes has an expression that makes it difficult to understand what he is thinking, but his innocence makes him a soothing presence to those around him. He is very curious and shows interest in everything, especially learning new things. He is highly sensitive and sensitive to the feelings of others, but he is not good at asserting himself and sometimes has difficulty expressing his opinions.
Concern: Delivery dates in this city have a way of drifting once the diggers arrive, and the ground here has surprised us before. Before anyone commits, I want to know what this site and the handful of firms willing to work here will really let us finish.

Name: Shizue
Age: 78
Gender: female
Personality: Shizue has a very calm and gentle personality. Even as she has grown older, she continues to smile warmly at those around her and is a very caring person. She is always considerate of others, friendly, and sometimes shows a playful side. She often reaches out to those who are feeling down with kind words and never hesitates to lend a helping hand when needed, which has earned her the affection of many people in the village and community. Through her years of life experience, Shizue has come to understand the importance of living peacefully with others.
Concern: Something in how this city commissions work keeps producing handsome openings and short lives. I would rather judge by what the last decade of our schemes looks like now than by drawings.

Name: Shunichi
Age: 32
Gender: male
Personality: Shunichi is a very confident person who can remain calm in any situation. He is not modest, and has a slightly sarcastic side, but that is part of his charm. He is not sociable, but he is good at communicating at the right time and is relied upon by those around him. He rarely becomes overly emotional and can analyze situations calmly and act accordingly, so he has an unexpectedly rational side.
Concern: This park is not an empty stage; it is crossed, drained, mown and rained on every week of the year. What worries me is that we pick something which reads well on paper and then fights the way the ground and the people here actually behave.

Name: Victoria
Age: 37
Gender: female
Personality: Victoria is a calm and rational person, but at times her excessive thoughtfulness can create barriers between her and those around her. She is reserved in her emotional expressions and keenly observes the expressions and attitudes of others, trying to discern their inner thoughts. Because she does not express herself much, she often gives others the impression of being somewhat mysterious, but deep down she has a strong will and a determination to stick to her beliefs. At times, she may display expressions of anxiety or fear, but it is precisely in such moments that her true strength becomes evident.
Concern: Every new thing the city opens lands on the same rota, and that rota is shorter each year. I am trying to work out who would really run and look after this place, week in and week out.

## Hidden information
The candidates and the full text of every card are listed here. The participants do not know them before the schedule above says so, and nothing from them may appear in the talk before the round in which it is revealed.

Candidates (see the schedule above):
- A: Woodland Walk. A plan that plants dense tree cover across the northern half of the site, threaded with gravel paths, small clearings, and a visitor shelter near the main gate.
- B: Market Plaza. A plan that creates a paved central square with stall infrastructure, shade structures, and utility connections intended for weekend markets and seasonal events.
- C: Sports Terraces. A plan that replaces the open lawn with multi-use courts, a marked running loop, changing facilities, and stepped seating along the southern side of the site.
- D: Wetland Restoration. A plan that reshapes the park's drainage into a series of ponds and reed beds, with boardwalks and observation points arranged along the water's edge.

Cards (see the schedule above; title: text):
- Terms of the regional habitat fund: Two thirds of the capital envelope comes from a regional habitat fund whose terms pay only for planting and water management, never for surfacing or buildings.
- Upkeep ledger spend per hectare: The upkeep ledger puts annual spend per hectare on planted and water-managed ground at roughly triple that of hard-surfaced areas, and the gap has widened yearly.
- Regional firms tendering for earth-moving: Only two regional firms still tender for bulk earth-moving; both flagged clay subsoil and slippage risk, though they quote shallow, small-plant work at ordinary rates.
- Depot phasing notes on hoarding the site: Phasing notes from the depot say the southern ground can be hoarded off in stages while the park stays open; the centre and the main gate cannot.
- Record of the eastern avenue planting: Half the young trees put in along the eastern avenue five years ago were dead by the second summer; aftercare watering had been left out of the contract.
- Condition of works from the earlier programme: The overflow basin cut upstream eight years back still needs no rebuild, while the apron resurfaced outside the civic hall in the same programme has been patched three times.
- Timed counts of weekday crossings: Timed counts on three weekday mornings found most people crossing the site to reach the tram stop, keeping to firm, open ground rather than the softer margins.
- Drainage callouts and August heat readings: Drainage callouts after storms have doubled since the culvert was capped, and heat readings taken last August ran several degrees above the shaded streets nearby.
- Groundskeeping roll and bought-in services: The groundskeeping roll has fallen from eighteen posts to seven; specialist water and turf care is bought in, while weekend stewarding is already covered by a casual pool.
- Volunteer groups working with the division: Two standing volunteer groups already work with the division most weekends, one on habitat tasks upriver and one lining and refereeing the youth league grounds.

Write the complete transcript of the discussion in the exact Markdown format specified. Output only the transcript.

## Output format
Markdown, exactly this structure; nothing before or after it:

# candidate_selection_0024
## Round 1
### Talk
#### Turn 1 of 4
- **<Name>**: <utterance, or exactly Skip, or exactly Over>
(one line per participant, in the fixed speaking order; repeat for Turn 2, 3 and 4; a participant who said Over has no line in the later turns of that round)
### Action
- investigate: <Name> -> <card title>; <card title>
(one line per participant; titles exactly as listed)
## Round 2
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
## Round 3
### Talk
(4 turns as above)
### Vote
- <voter name> -> <candidate label>
(one line per participant)
- adopted: <label of the candidate with the most votes>
## Result
- adopted: <label>
